paper_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: What is the composition of the hybrid electron-collecting buffer layer (ECBL) system used in the PBDB-T:IT-M solar cells described in this study?
qa_pairs.answer: The hybrid electron-collecting buffer layer (ECBL) system consists of a zinc oxide (ZnO) and poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (PEOz) blend (ZnO:PEOz) which is further modified with an additional PEOz interlayer.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: What annealing temperature was applied to the ZnO:PEOz/PEOz combination layers, and what is the practical advantage of this specific temperature?
qa_pairs.answer: The combination layers were processed at a low thermal annealing temperature of 100 °C. This low-temperature processing is advantageous because it is compatible with roll-to-roll fabrication on flexible substrates.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: What were the average and maximum power conversion efficiencies (PCE) for inverted PBDB-T:IT-M solar cells utilizing a 6 wt% PEOz hybrid combination layer?
qa_pairs.answer: The inverted PBDB-T:IT-M solar cells using the ZnO:PEOz (6 wt% PEOz) / PEOz combination layer achieved an average PCE of 10.11% and a maximum PCE of 10.59%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: How does the concentration of PEOz in the ZnO:PEOz hybrid layer influence the electrical resistance and current density of the PBDB-T:IT-M devices?
qa_pairs.answer: The inclusion of 6 wt% PEOz in the ZnO precursor minimizes the series resistance (Rs) to 0.13 kΩ. This reduction in resistance correlates with the highest observed short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 16.19 mA/cm², as Jsc was found to increase gradually with PEOz content up to the 6 wt% threshold.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: According to Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) results, how does the surface morphology of the ZnO:PEOz (6 wt%) layer facilitate electron transfer?
qa_pairs.answer: AFM revealed that the ZnO:PEOz (6 wt%) layer features a textured surface with nanocrater structures. These structures increase the interfacial contact area between the buffer layer and the bulk heterojunction (BHJ) layer, which enhances electron transfer from the active layer.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: Compare the degradation of short-circuit current density (Jsc) between devices using pristine ZnO and those using the ZnO:PEOz (6 wt%) hybrid layer after 12 hours of light exposure.
qa_pairs.answer: Under continuous one-sun illumination for 12 hours, the device with the pristine ZnO/PEOz layer (0 wt% PEOz) showed a significant Jsc reduction of 68.72%. In contrast, the device utilizing the ZnO:PEOz (6 wt%) / PEOz hybrid layer showed a much lower reduction of 35.27%, indicating significantly improved photostability.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: How does the 6 wt% PEOz hybrid combination layer affect the timeline for the appearance of sigmoidal (S-shape) J-V curves during continuous light exposure?
qa_pairs.answer: The use of the 6 wt% PEOz hybrid layer delays the appearance of the sigmoidal J-V curve, which indicates severe device degradation. While the pristine ZnO layer showed this S-shape after 2 hours of light exposure, the 6 wt% PEOz hybrid layer extended this time to 4 hours.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers

qa_pairs.question: What physical mechanism allows polymeric interlayers such as PEOz to increase the built-in potential of organic solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: Polymeric interlayers like PEOz function by creating dipoles on the metal oxide (ECBL) surface. This dipole formation modifies the work function of the layer, which subsequently increases the built-in potential of the device.
qa_pairs.source_title: Performance and Stability of Polymer: Nonfullerene Solar Cells with 100 °C-Annealed Electron-Collecting Combination Layers
